top_line: A study commissioned by King Willem-Alexander found that the House of Orange backed colonialism for centuries and earned the equivalent of about €576 million from it; the King called the findings "heartbreaking and confronting," and Prime Minister Rob Jetten ruled out new reparations.

stories.headline: Study: Dutch royal family earned about €576 million from colonialism; King calls the findings 'heartbreaking and confronting'
stories.summary: A five-volume, 2,000-page study of the House of Orange-Nassau's role in Dutch colonial history was presented to King Willem-Alexander on Friday at the Academy Building in Leiden. The King asked for the study and paid for it. About sixty researchers worked on it, led by Gert Oostindie. Oostindie said every stadtholder, king and queen, at least up to Queen Wilhelmina, was convinced colonialism was legitimate, and that they gave it 'active and unscrupulous' support for centuries. That included slavery for as long as it existed and the violent crushing of uprisings. The family earned the equivalent of nearly €576 million in today's money. About €566 million of that came from the Dutch East India Company (VOC) and the former Dutch East Indies, now Indonesia, and roughly half a billion euros came in the 19th century alone. Over two centuries the family also received about €86 million in allowances from colonial companies, tied to their official positions. The researchers say little of this money is left in the family's wealth today. Stadtholder William V fled the country penniless in 1795, and later fortunes were lost on investments in Tsarist Russia and the Habsburg empire. The Oranges made almost nothing from the transatlantic slave trade, but only because the West India Company lost them money, not because they objected to it. The researchers found the royals rarely set colonial policy themselves. The exception was King William I (who reigned 1813 to 1840), who largely ran colonial policy on his own and in 1828 looked for ways around laws against the slave trade. The study calls Queen Wilhelmina the most imperialist monarch. She backed the Aceh War and the military campaign against Indonesian independence, and in 1947 she wrote that she had no objection to 'police actions.' Criticism of colonialism from the palace began only with Queen Juliana in 1948. The King called the conclusions 'heartbreaking and confronting' and said they 'affect me.' He said, 'I cannot change the past, but I can make a positive contribution to the present and the future,' and called the report 'not a conclusion but a call to action.' He did not mention any financial repair. The research appears in three illustrated academic volumes, an English-language comparative book called 'European Monarchs & Colonialism,' and a book for the general public by Oostindie called 'Oranje en de Koloniën, 1600-2025.' The publisher, Boom, sells them. At his weekly press conference, Prime Minister Rob Jetten ruled out new reparations. He pointed to the €200 million the government set aside in 2023 for awareness, remembrance and education, and to plans to return colonial-era art. Reactions were mixed. NiNsee, the national institute for the history and legacy of Dutch slavery, welcomed the report and called for talks on repair. A foundation representing Indigenous people from Suriname and the Caribbean said they were once again overlooked. Activist Mitchell Esajas, co-founder of The Black Archives, returned the royal honour he received in 2023, saying 'words about reconciliation and connection are not enough' while economic and racial inequality persists.
stories.context: The Netherlands is a constitutional monarchy: the King is head of state, but elected governments make policy. That is why the study separates the monarchs' enthusiasm for colonialism from their limited power over it. Before 1813 the Dutch Republic was run by the States General (its assembly), with stadtholders from the House of Orange as hereditary leaders. The VOC, or Dutch East India Company, was a chartered trading company with its own armies that dominated what became the Dutch East Indies. The Dutch also held slave colonies in Suriname and the Caribbean through the West India Company. On 19 December 2022, then-Prime Minister Mark Rutte apologised on behalf of the government for slavery. He called it 'a comma, not a full stop,' and the government set aside €200 million. On 1 July 2023 (Keti Koti, the annual commemoration of abolition), the King apologised and asked forgiveness for his ancestors' failure to act. He has also stopped using the Golden Coach because of a panel showing colonial scenes. Researchers say no other European monarch has gone this far. The study's debate over reparations is similar to the one in the US about reparations for slavery. Rob Jetten, the current prime minister, leads D66, a centrist liberal party.
key_terms: Huis Oranje-Nassau (House of Orange-Nassau, the Dutch royal family)
Oranjes (the Oranges, informal name for the royals)
VOC – Verenigde Oostindische Compagnie (Dutch East India Company)
stadhouder (stadtholder, leader of the Dutch Republic before the monarchy)
NiNsee (National Institute for the Study of Dutch Slavery and its Legacy)
Keti Koti (annual commemoration of the abolition of slavery, 1 July)

findings.question: How is the €576 million total broken down? NOS cites about €500 million from the East Indies in the 19th century plus about €86 million in allowances. What base year and method did the researchers use to convert to today's euros?
findings.answer: News agency reporting (via ZeelandNet) says that of the roughly €576 million total, about €566 million came from the former Dutch East Indies (via the VOC and later colonial revenues). NOS and Omroep West report about half a billion euros of this was earned in the 19th century. Separately, about €86 million came from allowances paid by colonial companies over two centuries, tied to the family's official positions. €500m plus €86m is more than €576m, so the allowances probably overlap with the total, but no source spells this out. None of the coverage gives the base year or conversion method; outlets just say the sums were 'converted' (omgerekend) into today's euros. NOS and the researchers add that the profits barely contribute to the royal family's current wealth: William V fled penniless in 1795, and historian Idesbald Goddeeris (VRT) says later money was lost in Tsarist Russian and Habsburg investments.

findings.question: DutchNews headlined the €576 million as earned 'from slavery,' while NOS and NU.nl describe it as profit from colonialism, mostly the East Indies. Which framing does the report itself use?
findings.answer: The researchers and Leiden University describe it as profit from colonialism: the Oranges 'profited more from colonialism than they shaped it,' with about half a billion euros in today's money earned mainly in the 19th century, mostly via the VOC and the Dutch East Indies. Slavery is treated as part of the colonialism the family supported ('including slavery while it existed'), not as the source of the income; the family earned almost nothing from the transatlantic slave trade. DutchNews.nl's 'from slavery' headline is its own framing; even its article says the money came predominantly from the East Indies.

findings.question: Has the royal palace or the King said anything about using any of the family's wealth for repair or restitution?
findings.answer: No. The King's official reaction, published by the Royal House, does not mention family wealth, restitution or compensation. He spoke of 'connection, healing and reconciliation' and said: 'I cannot change the past, but I can make a positive contribution to the present and the future.' The government, through PM Jetten, ruled out new reparations.

findings.question: What has the €200 million set aside by the government in 2023 actually been spent on so far?
findings.answer: According to the government, the €200 million is split in two. €100 million is for government measures: changes to primary and secondary education, research, museums and protecting cultural heritage in all the countries involved. The other €100 million is for subsidies to civil society initiatives. A Commemoration Committee for Slavery Heritage was set up in early 2025. The final subsidy rules were published on 1 July 2025, and the first application round opened on 11 August 2025. I found no figures for how much has actually been paid out so far.

findings.question: Are the five books freely available online, as the King said he wanted, and what are their titles?
findings.answer: The titles are: 'Van Willem de Zwijger tot Willem-Alexander' (biographical volume), 'Koloniale macht, profijt en prestige' and 'Schaduwen van de Oranjezon' (thematic volumes), 'European Monarchs & Colonialism' (international comparison, in English), and the book for the general public, 'Oranje en de Koloniën, 1600-2025. De koloniale geschiedenis van het Huis Oranje-Nassau', with an English edition, 'The Dutch Monarchy and Its Colonial History, 1600–2025'. The King said the results 'must become available to everyone', but I could not confirm a free or open-access online version. Boom publishes the books commercially: the set costs €99.90 and single volumes €29.90–€39.90.

stories.airtime_reason: Lead with the most to unpack: the money breakdown, Wilhelmina and William I, the gap between what the royals wanted and what they could decide, the King's words, Jetten's 'no' on reparations, and the split reactions, including the honour sent back

stories.headline: Dutch inflation rises to 3.4% on fuel prices; G7 releases up to 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel
stories.summary: Dutch inflation rose to 3.4 percent in September, up from 3.3 percent in August, according to a first estimate from the statistics bureau CBS. Final figures are due on 13 October. Fuel and energy drove most of the increase: motor fuel and heating energy cost 13.9 percent more than a year earlier, and electricity is now also more expensive than last year. Groceries got cheaper for a second month in a row, down 1.3 percent year on year. CBS chief economist Peter Hein van Mulligen warned that high energy prices usually show up in shop prices after about six months, but he does not expect a spike like 2022. Inflation in the eurozone rose to 3.8 percent, its highest level since September 2023. Before the war in Iran began, it was just under 2 percent. Advisory pump prices for diesel and petrol are above €2.70 a litre, although the average price people actually pay at the pump is lower. Separately, the G7 countries agreed in a video call led by French President Emmanuel Macron to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves over the next four months, coordinated by the International Energy Agency (IEA). Under a French proposal, European countries would supply 50 million barrels of diesel and IEA members 50 million barrels of crude. A large share of the diesel is to be released in the first 20 days. No breakdown by country has been published yet. The decision followed pressure from US President Donald Trump, who had threatened to ban US diesel exports to lower prices at home ahead of the US midterm elections. Europe now gets much of its diesel from the US. European diesel futures fell about 8 percent after the announcement. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen welcomed the decision. The Netherlands is already drawing on its own reserves under the earlier IEA agreement from March. On Thursday the cabinet released a third batch of about 753,000 barrels, mostly diesel and petrol. That brings the Dutch total to nearly 4.7 million of the 5.4 million barrels it pledged. The government has not said whether it will add to that under the new G7 deal. On fuel tax, the cabinet announced on Budget Day that it will spend €750 million to phase out the existing fuel excise discount more slowly in 2027, rather than cut excise duty further.
stories.context: CBS (Statistics Netherlands) is the government's statistics bureau, similar to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics. Eurostat is the EU's statistics office. The European Central Bank aims for inflation of about 2 percent. Many Dutch households remember 2022, when energy prices after Russia's invasion of Ukraine pushed Dutch inflation to double digits. Europe used to import diesel mainly from Russia and the Middle East, which is why a US export ban would have hurt. The G7 is made up of the US, Canada, the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Japan. The Netherlands is not a member, but it is an IEA member and takes part in joint stock releases. In March, the IEA's 32 members agreed on a record 400 million-barrel release because of the Iran conflict, and about two-thirds of it has already been released.
key_terms: CBS – Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (Statistics Netherlands)
Peter Hein van Mulligen (CBS chief economist)

findings.question: How many of the 100 million barrels will come from European, and specifically Dutch, emergency stocks? Reuters sources mentioned 50 million barrels of diesel from Europe.
findings.answer: Reporting based on Reuters describes a French proposal for European countries to release 50 million barrels of diesel and for IEA members to release 50 million barrels of crude, which together make up the 100 million. No country-by-country breakdown has been published, and no Dutch share of the G7 release has been announced. Separately, on 1 October the Dutch government released a third batch under the March IEA agreement. It was 95 kilotons, about 753,000 barrels: 50 kt diesel and 45 kt petrol. That brings the Dutch total to nearly 4.7 million of the 5.4 million barrels pledged, about 87 percent. Autobahn.eu stresses that this release falls under the March agreement, not the new US request.

findings.question: Reuters reported a 20-day timeline for diesel, while NOS reports a four-month window for the full release. Which applies to what?
findings.answer: Both are correct. The full release of up to 100 million barrels runs over four months, starting immediately. Within that, the G7 statement calls for 'a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days' by G7 members and partners.

findings.question: How large are the Netherlands' strategic oil and diesel reserves, and has the Dutch government said whether it will draw on them?
findings.answer: The Dutch obligation is the larger of 90 days of net imports or 61 days of domestic consumption. For 2025-2026, the stockholding agency COVA must hold at least 4,100 kilotons crude oil equivalent. That includes 913 kt of diesel/gasoil, 229 kt of petrol and 16 kt of kerosene. Companies must hold another 653 kt. The government is already drawing on these stocks under the March IEA action: releases in late July, early September and from 2 October total nearly 4.7 million of the 5.4 million barrels pledged. Kerosene is being held back. No statement has been found on whether the Netherlands will contribute more under the new G7 deal.

findings.question: Is the Dutch government considering cutting fuel excise duty to ease pump prices above €2.70?
findings.answer: No new excise cut has been announced. On Budget Day in September 2026, the cabinet set aside €750 million to phase out the existing excise discount more slowly in 2027. That prevents a planned rise of about 12 cents a litre on diesel but does not lower excise. Current excise is about 84.5 cents a litre on petrol and 55.2 cents on diesel. One caveat on prices: €2.70+ is the advisory pump price. Autobahn.eu reported an advisory price of €2.769 against an actual average of €2.526 on 28 September.

stories.airtime_reason: Two connected developments: inflation numbers people feel at the pump and the G7 diesel release forced by Trump's export threat. Needs some background on the IEA and Dutch reserves

stories.headline: Court rules stricter family reunification rules also apply to applications filed before the change
stories.summary: The district court in The Hague has ruled that stricter rules for bringing family members to the Netherlands also apply to applications filed before the rules took effect. The case was brought by two Syrians with 'subsidiary protection' status. This means they are not recognised as refugees but cannot safely return home. The immigration service (IND) rejected their requests to bring over relatives under the new conditions, which took effect on 12 June with the EU Asylum and Migration Pact. Under the new two-status system, people with subsidiary protection must wait two years before applying and must have housing suitable for the whole family. The law has no transitional arrangement, so the changes also apply to applications that were still pending. When the rules took effect, more than 19,000 people were waiting for an IND decision on family reunification. It is not clear how many of them have subsidiary protection. In its rulings, issued on 2 October, the court acknowledged the effects can be serious, especially for people who applied under the old rules. Even so, it found that the new rules and their application to older cases do not violate higher law or general legal principles. It is the court's first ruling on the new rules. The Syrians' lawyer will appeal, and the refugee charity VluchtelingenWerk Nederland said the Council of State will have the final word. No date has been given for that ruling. About 150,000 Syrians live in the Netherlands. Since Assad's fall in late 2024, at least 1,440 have returned voluntarily, with adults offered €3,000 and children €1,800.
stories.context: Family reunification (nareis) lets people granted asylum bring over spouses and children. Restricting it has been a central goal of Dutch parties pushing for tougher migration policy. The EU Asylum and Migration Pact, which took effect across the EU in June 2026, aims to standardise and speed up asylum procedures. The Netherlands used it to bring in a 'two-status system' that treats recognised refugees more generously than people with subsidiary protection. The IND is the Immigration and Naturalisation Service, roughly comparable to US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). Ter Apel is the main asylum registration centre. The Raad van State (Council of State) is the highest court for cases against the government, so it will settle the question.
key_terms: IND – Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst (Immigration and Naturalisation Service)
Europees asiel- en migratiepact (EU Asylum and Migration Pact)
Rechtbank Den Haag (The Hague District Court)
Raad van State (Council of State, top administrative court)
open_questions: When is the Council of State expected to rule on the appeal?

findings.question: How many pending family reunification applications filed before 12 June are affected by this ruling?
findings.answer: No source gives an exact number of pending pre-12 June applications affected by this ruling. When the new rules took effect on 12 June 2026, the Reformatorisch Dagblad reported that more than 19,000 people were waiting for an IND decision on family reunification. It did not say how many of them had subsidiary protection rather than refugee status. The two-status law has no transitional arrangement, so the new rules apply immediately to pending applications. The court's rulings (ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2026:28901 and 28902, dated 2 October 2026) do not give a figure either.

findings.question: When is the Council of State expected to rule on the appeal?
Which parties do ministers Van den Brink (Asylum and Migration) and Berendsen (Foreign Affairs) belong to?
findings.answer: Both belong to the CDA (Christian Democratic Appeal). Bart van den Brink is Minister of Asylum and Migration and second deputy prime minister. Tom Berendsen has been Minister of Foreign Affairs since 23 February 2026. Both are in the Jetten cabinet.

stories.airtime_reason: A real fairness question (new rules applied to old applications), and subsidiary protection needs explaining. An appeal is pending and there are few figures

stories.headline: Rabobank and ABN Amro cut how much older buyers can borrow for a mortgage
stories.summary: Two of the largest Dutch banks are tightening mortgage rules for older borrowers. From March 2027, Rabobank and its subsidiary Obvion will base the maximum mortgage on expected pension income starting 15 years before retirement instead of 10. With the retirement age at 67, that affects applicants from age 52. Rabobank will also factor in life expectancy: borrowers aged 85 and over will be able to borrow at most 70 percent of their home's value. The rules apply to new customers and to people refinancing or changing an existing Rabobank mortgage, but not to existing loans that stay unchanged. ABN Amro and its mortgage label Florius will bring in similar changes on 9 December 2026, according to InFinance. ABN Amro will keep the 10-year pension threshold but check whether income after retirement is enough if the retirement date falls within the loan term. It will cap borrowing at age 85 at 50 percent of the home's value. The changes follow new industry-wide guidance from the Dutch central bank, DNB. It expects banks to check whether pension income can carry the loan when the loan runs past retirement. It also treats any part of a loan that outlasts the borrower's remaining life expectancy as comparable to interest-only debt, to be repaid mainly from selling the home. Others in the sector expect more lenders to follow, especially once the National Mortgage Guarantee (NHG) changes its conditions. ING has not announced any changes yet. The mortgage data firm IEX calculated that self-employed people with little pension savings will be hit hardest: someone relying only on the state pension may qualify for a mortgage of about 100,000 euros.
stories.context: Mortgages in the Netherlands are tightly regulated. Each year the government sets national limits on how much people can borrow based on income, and Dutch mortgages typically run 30 years. As pension income is usually lower than salary, counting it earlier lowers the maximum loan for people in their 50s. This matters in a housing market where prices are high and older buyers often move or refinance. DNB (De Nederlandsche Bank) is the central bank and banking supervisor, roughly like the US Federal Reserve in its supervisory role. Rabobank (with Obvion), ING and ABN Amro dominate the Dutch mortgage market.
key_terms: DNB – De Nederlandsche Bank (Dutch central bank)
open_questions: Roughly how much lower will the maximum mortgage be for a typical 55-year-old buyer under the new rules?

findings.question: What exactly do DNB's new guidelines require, and will ING and other lenders follow with similar changes?
findings.answer: DNB issued sector-wide guidance after talks with supervisors about how expected pension income and life expectancy count in mortgage assessments. DNB expects banks to check whether income after retirement is enough when the loan runs past that point. If a loan runs longer than the borrower's remaining life expectancy, DNB treats the outstanding part as economically comparable to interest-only debt, which makes the home's sale value an important source of repayment. TPO reports that this assessment method was the subject of intensive negotiations in recent years, and that the sector expects other lenders to follow, particularly once the National Mortgage Guarantee (NHG) adjusts its conditions. No source found reports any announcement or reaction from ING. ABN Amro's changes also apply to its Florius label.

findings.question: Roughly how much lower will the maximum mortgage be for a typical 55-year-old buyer under the new rules?

stories.airtime_reason: A concrete change with clear trade-offs: who loses borrowing power, the hit to self-employed people, DNB's reasoning about life expectancy. No typical-buyer number

stories.headline: Government plans excise tax on vapes from 2029
stories.summary: Vapes and refills will cost more from 1 January 2029, when the government plans to add an excise tax on top of the 21 percent VAT users already pay. The rate has not been set yet, but the aim is to make vapes about as expensive as tobacco. 'It is shocking how many young people are vaping,' said State Secretary for Finance Eelco Eerenberg of D66. In the latest national schools survey, from 2025, more than one in five pupils aged 12 to 16 (21.5 percent) had ever used a vape, 12.4 percent had vaped in the past month, and 4 percent vaped daily. Eerenberg said higher prices would make consumers think twice before spending money on 'unhealthy junk' and that 'the health of our children cannot wait for Brussels.' He admitted vapes are easy to buy online or across the border, so the government still hopes for an EU-wide tax. If one takes effect before 2029, the Dutch proposal will be withdrawn. An EU-wide tax looks unlikely soon, though. The European Commission proposed in July 2025 to extend EU tobacco taxes to e-cigarette liquids, with a planned start in 2028. Tax rules need the backing of all 27 member states, and in June 2026 EU finance ministers dropped the plan from their agenda because they could not all agree. Ireland, which now chairs the EU Council, has taken over the file. The Dutch bill is expected to go to the House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer) as a separate bill in early 2027, not as part of the annual Tax Plan. Flavoured vapes other than tobacco flavour have been banned since January 2024, smoking bans also cover vaping, and vape sales are expected to be limited to specialist shops from July 2027 or January 2028.
stories.context: A state secretary (staatssecretaris) is a junior minister responsible for one area within a ministry. At Finance, that area usually includes taxes. Excise duties are per-product taxes, like US federal and state cigarette taxes, added on top of VAT (btw). The Netherlands has steadily tightened rules on smoking and vaping, and in practice the national flavour ban is often ignored. The EU has long discussed updating its tobacco tax directive to cover e-cigarettes.
key_terms: staatssecretaris van Financiën (state secretary for Finance)

findings.question: Which party does State Secretary Eelco Eerenberg belong to? NL Times also spells his name 'Eerenburg', so which spelling is correct?
findings.answer: He belongs to D66 and serves as State Secretary for Finance in the Jetten cabinet. The correct spelling is 'Eerenberg', as used by NOS, Parlement.com, D66 and the municipality of Utrecht, where he was previously an alderman. He was nominated after Nathalie van Berkel withdrew over inaccuracies in her CV. The NL Times article on this story also spells it 'Eerenberg'.

findings.question: Where does the EU proposal to tax e-cigarettes stand, and when might it take effect?
findings.answer: In July 2025 the European Commission proposed revising the Tobacco Taxation Directive so that EU minimum excise rates would also cover newer products, including e-cigarette liquids. The proposed start date was 1 January 2028. EU tax rules need unanimous agreement in the Council. On 3 June 2026 the European Parliament's economics committee approved a scaled-back version with lower rates and longer transition periods for e-cigarettes and other new products, in some cases running to 2034. The same day, the dossier was taken off the agenda of the 12 June Ecofin meeting because member states could not all agree. The Irish Council Presidency has taken over the file. I found no later agreement, so there is no firm date for an EU-wide vape tax.

findings.question: How many Dutch young people vape, according to the latest figures?
findings.answer: The most recent schools survey is Trimbos's 2025 HBSC study. Among secondary school pupils aged 12 to 16, 21.5 percent had ever used a vape, 12.4 percent had vaped in the past month and 4.0 percent vaped daily. Girls vape more than boys: 15.8 percent of girls had vaped in the past month, against 9.2 percent of boys. Among young adults aged 18 to 24, 8.1 percent regularly used an e-cigarette in 2025.

stories.airtime_reason: Youth vaping figures, the 'Brussels can't wait' angle and the stuck EU process make a decent story, even though the tax starts in 2029 and has no rate yet

stories.headline: Amsterdam drops plan to make Utrechtsestraat one-way
stories.summary: Amsterdam has dropped its plan to make Utrechtsestraat a one-way street, Het Parool reports. The idea was announced earlier this year. The city said the street was unsafe and that more than 4,200 vehicles a day used it. Southbound traffic would have kept the street, running from Rembrandtplein to Frederiksplein, and northbound traffic would have been sent through side streets. Strong objections from residents changed the city's mind. Several neighbourhood groups feared the plan would push traffic onto nearby streets. They also challenged the city's traffic figures and did their own counts. A neighbourhood survey found that most respondents felt the street was safe and were against one-way traffic. The small-business group MKB Metropool Amsterdam also opposed the plan. In a letter to residents, the city said it will try smaller safety measures instead. These include an extra zebra crossing, changes at the junction with Frederiksplein, targeted checks on loading and unloading, speed checks and speed bumps. This is still a proposed decision by the executive board of the Centrum district. The district committee will discuss it and give its advice on Monday 6 October, before a final decision is taken.
stories.context: Utrechtsestraat is a busy shopping and restaurant street in central Amsterdam. It runs from Rembrandtplein across the canal ring toward Frederiksplein, and trams, cyclists, delivery vehicles and pedestrians all share it. The city has been reshaping inner-city streets to cut car traffic and give more space to cyclists and pedestrians, and such plans often run into objections from shopkeepers and residents.
open_questions: Which alderman (wethouder) is responsible for the decision?

findings.question: Why did the City of Amsterdam drop the one-way plan for Utrechtsestraat? Were there objections from shopkeepers, residents or the tram operator GVB?
findings.answer: Opposition from residents was the main reason. Several neighbourhood groups feared that one-way traffic would push cars onto surrounding streets. They also disputed the city's count of more than 4,200 vehicles a day and carried out their own counts. A survey by the neighbourhood group N8W8 drew more than 500 responses: 81% said the street felt safe and 88% opposed one-way traffic. The ASVO primary school worried about more traffic on its street. The business association MKB Metropool Amsterdam opposed the plan in May 2026. None of the sources mention any objection from the tram operator GVB. In February the traffic alderman said removing the tram was not part of the plan.

findings.question: What was the original plan for Utrechtsestraat, and what will happen to the street instead?
findings.answer: The plan was presented in early 2026 (February) to deal with traffic danger and heavy traffic. Under it, Utrechtsestraat would have been one-way going south, from Rembrandtplein to Frederiksplein. Northbound traffic would have been sent along other routes, such as Achtergracht and Reguliersgracht. Instead, the city plans smaller measures: changes at the Utrechtsestraat–Frederiksplein junction, an extra zebra crossing, enforcement against illegal loading and parking, speed checks (possibly with speed cameras) and physical traffic calming such as speed bumps. The city announced this in an email to residents on 29 September 2026. It is still a proposed decision. The Centrum district committee will discuss it and give advice on 6 October, and the district executive will then make the final decision.

findings.question: Which alderman (wethouder) is responsible for the decision?

stories.airtime_reason: A local street plan reversed by resident pressure. Easy to picture, but it doesn't take long to tell

stories.headline: 'Truly Naked' sweeps the Golden Calf film awards; Van Basten series 'Basta' wins three
stories.summary: The drama Truly Naked, the first feature by Dutch director Muriel d'Ansembourg, won six of its seven nominations at the Golden Calf gala in Utrecht. Its awards were best film, director, screenplay, editing, cinematography and production design. The English-language film is about how pornography affects teenage lives and follows Alec, an introverted British boy growing up in his father's low-budget porn business. It premiered at the Berlin film festival and opened in Dutch cinemas on 23 April. It can now be streamed on services including Pathé Thuis and Picl. Basta, a Videoland series about football star Marco van Basten that started streaming on 4 September, won best drama series, best direction and best lead actor for Chris Peters. Joe Speedboot, the favourite with nine nominations, won only one: Daan Buringa took best lead actor in a feature film for playing the silent, wheelchair-using Fransje Hermans. Halina Reijn, director of the Nicole Kidman film Babygirl, received the career award for film culture and called herself 'a farmer's girl in Hollywood.' Other winners included This Is Your Captain Speaking (best short), Maasja Ooms' Mijn woord tegen het mijne (best documentary) and a posthumous make-up award for Katja Alexis. The audience awards went to Voor de meisjes and Mama'ku – Van Jakarta tot de Molukken. The 46th gala closed the Netherlands Film Festival.
stories.context: The Gouden Kalveren (Golden Calves) are the Netherlands' top film and TV prizes, a mix of the Oscars and the Emmys handed out at the end of the Netherlands Film Festival in Utrecht each autumn. Marco van Basten is one of the greatest Dutch footballers. He starred for Ajax and AC Milan and scored the famous volley in the 1988 European Championship final, which is the Dutch national team's only major title. Joe Speedboot is adapted from a much-loved novel by Tommy Wieringa. Halina Reijn is one of the few Dutch directors with a Hollywood career.
key_terms: Gouden Kalf / Gouden Kalveren (Golden Calf awards)
Nederlands Film Festival (Netherlands Film Festival, Utrecht)

findings.question: When will Truly Naked be in Dutch cinemas or on streaming, and is it in English?
findings.answer: The film is already out. It opened in Dutch cinemas on 23 April 2026, after premiering in the Perspectives section of the 2026 Berlinale. It is in English and set in a British seaside town. It is a Dutch–Belgian–French co-production lasting 102 minutes, produced by Isabella Films in Amsterdam, and Paradiso distributes it in the Netherlands. FilmVandaag lists it as streaming on Pathé Thuis and Picl. Dutch Wikipedia dates the Berlin premiere to 16 February 2025, but that looks like a mistake, since the other sources place it at the 2026 Berlinale.

findings.question: Where can Basta be watched, on which broadcaster or streamer?
findings.answer: Basta is a Videoland Original series. Videoland is RTL's Dutch streaming service, and the series has been available there since 4 September 2026.

stories.airtime_reason: Gives the hosts things to recommend: an English-language winner that's streamable, the Van Basten series with backstory, the upset of the favourite, and Halina Reijn's 'farmer's girl' line

stories.headline: Optician chain Hans Anders pulls Meta's camera glasses from its shops
stories.summary: Hans Anders, the Dutch optician chain, has stopped selling Meta's AI camera glasses in its shops and webshop for now, first reported by the newspaper AD. A spokesperson cited the 'public and political discussions about smart glasses' and questions about the conditions under which the technology can be used. The chain had sold only 'limited numbers' of the glasses, which Meta developed with Ray-Ban and which cost at least €419. They look like normal glasses but can take photos and video hands-free, make calls and play music, with a small light flickering while recording. On Tuesday, abuse victims' support group Offlimits and campaign group The Firewall gave Meta two weeks to stop selling the glasses. They say the glasses make covert filming easy and lead to privacy violations, and they threaten to go to court if Meta does not comply. NOS also reported that the Consumentenbond, the Dutch consumers' association, is involved. The same day, the House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer) passed a motion asking the cabinet to further restrict wearing what critics call 'peeping glasses,' with exceptions for medical use. The cabinet has so far been reluctant: Justice State Secretary Van Bruggen prefers to wait for an EU assessment of camera glasses, expected this autumn. Other retailers, including Pearle, Specsavers, MediaMarkt and Ray-Ban stores, are still selling the glasses. Hans Anders will decide later whether the glasses return.
stories.context: The Netherlands takes privacy seriously. Strict EU data protection law (the GDPR) applies, and Dutch law already penalises secretly filming people in sexual or degrading situations. Hans Anders is a familiar budget optician on Dutch shopping streets, like a LensCrafters. The nickname 'gluurbril' ('peeping glasses') shows how the debate has been framed in the Netherlands.

findings.question: Which Dutch organisations have threatened to sue Meta over its smart glasses, and on what legal grounds?
findings.answer: On 29 September 2026, Stichting Offlimits (a support organisation for victims of online abuse) and The Firewall (a group campaigning against Big Tech) gave Meta two weeks to stop selling the glasses. Cloud Expo reports the demand was also addressed to EssilorLuxottica. They are threatening summary proceedings (kort geding). Their grounds are privacy: the right to privacy under European law and the unlawful processing of images of people who have not consented. They argue the glasses make covert filming easy and encourage privacy violations and online harassment. They demand that Meta withdraw the product while it can record secretly, and that it stop processing recordings made without consent. NOS also names the Consumentenbond as one of the organisations involved. Separately, on the same day, the journalists' union NVJ, the Auteursbond and Lira made demands of Meta over copyright and AI training data. That dispute is not about the glasses.

findings.question: Did the Tweede Kamer pass a motion calling for a ban on camera glasses, and how has the government responded?
findings.answer: Yes. On Tuesday 29 September 2026 the Tweede Kamer adopted a motion from PRO, CDA, D66, PvdD, SP, ChristenUnie, Volt, 50Plus and MP Keijzer. It asks the cabinet to further restrict the wearing of camera glasses and to work out legal options with the Dutch Data Protection Authority, with exceptions for necessary medical use. Results are due in the first quarter of next year. The cabinet is not obliged to follow the motion. Justice and Security State Secretary Van Bruggen had earlier refused to investigate a ban, preferring to wait for European privacy regulators. NOS reports the cabinet thinks a ban goes too far and is waiting for European guidance on camera and AI glasses, expected this autumn.

findings.question: Are other Dutch retailers, such as Pearle, Specsavers or MediaMarkt, still selling the Meta Ray-Ban glasses?
findings.answer: Yes. According to NOS, Pearle, Specsavers, MediaMarkt and Ray-Ban stores are still selling the glasses online and in their shops.

stories.airtime_reason: A lively privacy fight: one chain pulls the glasses while others keep selling, plus a threatened lawsuit, a parliament motion, a hesitant cabinet and the 'peeping glasses' nickname

stories.headline: Dutch television turns 75
stories.summary: The first Dutch television broadcast aired 75 years ago this week. It was a 90-minute live programme from a studio in Bussum, introduced by announcer Jeanne Roos, featuring a live performance of the play De Toverspiegel ('The Magic Mirror'). Thousands watched through radio shop windows or in cafés, and the royal family watched at Soestdijk Palace. There were only about 500 sets in the country, each costing 785 guilders, about a third of an average yearly income. Prime Minister Willem Drees wanted money spent on housing, not luxuries, and feared TV would distract workers and corrupt young people. Father Kors, who headed the broadcasters, warned on air about television's harmful influence. The government gave in only after Philips, the Eindhoven electronics company, threatened to set up television itself. Even then it was approved as a two-year experiment. A second channel followed in 1964 and a third in 1988. Media historian Huub Wijfjes says TV peaked in the 1960s to 1980s, when shows drew 7 to 8 million viewers, and remains 'the dominant medium.'
stories.context: The Netherlands started TV late. The BBC had broadcast since 1936 and the US had a postwar TV boom, and the Dutch started only one day after Denmark. Dutch public broadcasting is still organised around member-based broadcasting associations, historically tied to religious and political groups (Catholic KRO, socialist VARA and others). This reflects 'pillarisation' (verzuiling), the system in which Dutch society was divided into separate Catholic, Protestant, socialist and liberal groups, each with its own institutions. It explains why public TV here is shared among many broadcasters rather than run by a single BBC-style network. Old broadcasts can be watched at the Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision in Hilversum.
key_terms: NTS (Nederlandse Televisie Stichting, the first Dutch TV foundation)
Bussum (town near Hilversum, site of the first studio)
Beeld en Geluid (Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision)
stories.airtime_reason: Rich back-story about Dutch life: Drees's resistance, the Philips threat, Father Kors and 'pillarisation', which explains Dutch broadcasting today

events.name: Concertgebouw Orchestra: Classics Live
events.blurb: The Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, conducted by Iván Fischer and presented by Dominic Seldis, plays classical highlights in an arena. The night ends with Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, and the whole audience is invited to sing along in the famous 'Ode to Joy' finale.
events.note: Tickets via mojo.nl/kco; ticket holders get practice material ahead of time if they want to join the singing

events.name: Camera Japan Festival
events.when: Saturday 3 October, 12:30–22:00 (festival runs Thursday 1 to Sunday 4 October)
events.blurb: The largest Japanese film festival in the Benelux, showing arthouse, anime, LGBTQ+ and classic films, along with Japanese visual art, music, dance and food. It's an easy way to spend an afternoon or evening at a cosy cinema in Oud-West.
events.note: Second-to-last day; the organisers say 2026 times may still change, so check the Camera Japan website

events.name: Oosterkerk antique, curiosities and vintage market
events.blurb: A one-day market for antiques, curiosities and vintage finds in and around the Oosterkerk church. It's free to browse and a nice way to explore a quieter corner of the city on a Saturday morning.
